forces.title: Elevated Mortgage Rates and Input Costs Constrain Residential Sector
forces.description: The UK residential sector is facing substantial headwinds due to persistently high mortgage rates, which increase the cost of borrowing for prospective homeowners. Simultaneously, elevated input costs contribute to higher construction and property prices, further deterring demand. These factors collectively reduce affordability and slow down activity in the housing market, directly impacting the volume and profitability of housing finance products in the UK.
forces.source_title: Q3 UK economic outlook: Growth holds, inflation bites

forces.title: AI to Transform Mortgage Origination, Shifting from Brokers
forces.description: UK financial institutions need to embrace AI to fundamentally change mortgage origination. The shift involves moving away from traditional broker reliance towards offering real-time, pre-approved mortgage offers, triggered by customer behavioral signals. This structural change aims to foster stronger direct customer relationships, streamline processes, and create new revenue growth opportunities by making lending viable for broader segments and at smaller ticket sizes, enhancing the housing finance sector.
forces.source_title: The UK Financial Services Sector Has Lost Its Edge—Here’s How to Win It Back

forces.title: AI-Powered Credit Models Expand Addressable Housing Lending Market
forces.description: Leveraging more granular, AI-powered credit models presents a significant upside for the housing finance sector. These advanced models can enable lenders to expand their addressable market, making housing loans viable for smaller ticket sizes and to asset-light businesses that traditional cost structures might previously exclude. This enhances financial inclusion and opens new growth avenues within mortgage lending, improving accuracy in default prediction and reducing processing costs.
forces.source_title: The UK Financial Services Sector Has Lost Its Edge—Here’s How to Win It Back

forces.title: Institutionalized Regulatory Risk Aversion Limits Product Access
forces.description: UK regulation has institutionalized risk aversion among financial services, leading to consumer regulations that have unintentionally reduced access to certain financial products and investment advice. For the housing finance sector, this poses a risk of constraining the availability of diverse mortgage products or related advisory services, potentially making it harder for consumers to navigate and access suitable housing finance solutions due to a more cautious lending environment.
forces.source_title: The UK Financial Services Sector Has Lost Its Edge—Here’s How to Win It Back

forces.title: UK Financial Services Lagging in Technology Investment
forces.description: UK financial services firms have chronically under-invested in technology, particularly in software capital stock, which has grown significantly slower than in the US. This technological lag poses a substantial headwind to the sector's competitiveness and ability to innovate. For housing finance, this means slower adoption of efficiency-gaining technologies like AI-driven underwriting or advanced customer engagement platforms, potentially hindering efforts to reduce costs, expand market reach, and improve customer experience compared to global peers.
forces.source_title: The UK Financial Services Sector Has Lost Its Edge—Here’s How to Win It Back

viewpoints.title: UK Residential Sector Faces Significant Headwinds from High Mortgage Rates
viewpoints.description: The UK's residential sector is experiencing considerable challenges, primarily due to the impact of elevated input costs and persistently high mortgage rates. These financial pressures are creating a difficult environment for housing activity, affecting both potential homebuyers and developers. The high cost of borrowing directly constrains demand for housing finance and influences affordability, leading to subdued market conditions. This outlook suggests a period of sustained pressure on mortgage lending and related housing transactions in the near term.
viewpoints.source_title: Q3 UK economic outlook: Growth holds, inflation bites

viewpoints.title: Banks Need to Revolutionize Mortgage Origination with AI and Direct Offers
viewpoints.description: UK banks are urged to transform their mortgage origination processes by moving away from heavy reliance on brokers. The recommended shift involves leveraging AI to generate real-time, pre-approved mortgage offers based on customer behavioral signals. This strategic change aims to enhance direct customer relationships, improve efficiency, and potentially reverse the erosion of direct customer engagement caused by intermediation. Adopting this AI-driven approach is seen as crucial for banks to re-establish a competitive edge in the housing finance market.
viewpoints.source_title: The UK Financial Services Sector Has Lost Its Edge—Here’s How to Win It Back
